correctness.rationale: Two white vertices in the same true-twin clique can never be separated by any unique-neighbor force. With at most one white per clique, a force occurs precisely when the cyclic triple around the forcing clique contains two full and one partial clique; hence a full-index pair at distance at most two is necessary and sufficient. A pair creates an adjacent full pair then extends a full run around the cycle until all fill. Independent full-index sets in C_n^2 count failure configurations; their cyclic gap count a_nk=n/(n-2k) binom(n-2k,k) yields the polynomial. Exactly two full indices are necessary for minimum, and any three or more contain a removable full clique, proving well-forcedness and e_n m^(n-2). Exact direct zero-forcing enumeration and the C5[K3] 12-blue counter-witness corroborate small cases.
